prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: العربية · المنتجات (language ar, right-to-left: column 1 is on the RIGHT).
Grid: 4 columns × 5 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "المنتج" · longest unbreakable word 50px · one-line width 97px
  col 2: header "السعر" · longest unbreakable word 40px · one-line width 70px
  col 3: header "المخزون" · longest unbreakable word 53px · one-line width 53px
  col 4: header "الوصف" · longest unbreakable word 57px · one-line width 445px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 440px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 439px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 440px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"Arabic-language product inventory table for identifying each product, comparing price and stock, and reading a short description.","reading":"Right-to-left: the eye lands on the product name first, then scans the compact price and stock columns for comparison, then reads the description as secondary detail; each row should read as one product record.","groups":["col 1 (المنتج) is the row-label/identifier column and belongs on the right","col 2 (السعر) and col 3 (المخزون) form the numeric comparison group and should stay compact and adjacent","col 4 (الوصف) is free-text secondary content and can take the remaining width"],"keep_intact":["all four single-word headers","price numerals and currency unit (e.g. 3,200 ر.س)","stock values","product names where possible, especially model numbers such as 27 and 4K"],"may_wrap":["description text at word boundaries","product names at spaces in narrower designs","currency unit only if a price column is deliberately compressed, never split the numeral"]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[118,91,74,156],"idea":"Balanced: keep every product name and price on one line, keep the stock header intact, and give the remaining width to the description."},{"name":"B","widths":[85,91,74,189],"idea":"Description-first: let product names wrap at spaces so the description gets the widest measure and fewer lines."},{"name":"C","widths":[145,91,74,129],"idea":"Product-label priority: give the product column generous breathing room for fast row identification and accept a narrower, more-wrapped description."}]}
